description: We are Team SIRA Earth Intelligence from Dhaka, Bangladesh. We built **SIRA FireLab**, an evidence-led research workspace that analyzes NASA's microgravity combustion data. It combines data exploration, deterministic scientific analysis, source verification, and evidence synthesis to help researchers identify reliable findings and research gaps for future space research.
summary:
SIRA FireLab is an interactive, evidence-grounded research workspace for exploring NASA microgravity-combustion experiments relevant to human spaceflight.

It brings NASA PSI-69 FLEX Version 5 and PSI-25 BASS-II Study Version 4 into separate, provenance-preserving explorers, covering 274 and 129 experimental records respectively.

Researchers can inspect experimental conditions and measurement quality, run registered deterministic analyses, compare clearly bounded cohorts, and trace findings to source records through an Evidence Claim Ledger. The system preserves approximate and missing values, records exclusions, and exposes scientific limitations instead of overstating conclusions.

SIRA FireLab supports research for future Moon and Mars missions, but is not an operational firefighting tool or a certified spacecraft-safety model.
details:
SIRA FireLab addresses an important research challenge: NASA's microgravity combustion experiments contain valuable scientific evidence, but datasets, investigation records, and technical resources can be difficult to discover, inspect, and compare while preserving their original experimental context.

We developed an interactive research workspace with six main areas: Ask SIRA, Overview, Data Explorer, BASS-II Explorer, Research Lab, and Methods & Sources.

The platform integrates two NASA Physical Sciences Informatics investigations: PSI-69 FLEX Version 5, containing 274 experimental records, and PSI-25 BASS-II Study Version 4, containing 129 records. The investigations remain separate, preserving their individual provenance and scientific limitations.

Users can explore experimental records, inspect test conditions, review measurement quality, and run registered deterministic analyses. The system distinguishes exact, approximate, missing, and invalid measurements instead of silently treating them as equivalent.

Its research workflow connects questions, source records, calculations, evidence rankings, and findings through an Evidence Claim Ledger and scientific verification. Rankings remain limited to their declared metrics and cohorts. The system also identifies evidence gaps and uncertainties that require further investigation.

A key innovation is its evidence-first approach. Rather than relying on unrestricted chatbot-generated scientific conclusions, the deployed Ask SIRA feature uses bounded question classification, server-side evidence retrieval, and registered deterministic calculations. Generative explanations are disabled in this release.

The platform was developed using Python 3.10+, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Node.js for development and testing. It uses GitHub for source-code management and Microsoft Azure Container Apps for public deployment. No dedicated hardware was required.

SIRA FireLab aims to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, transparent, reproducible, and useful for future human exploration of the Moon and Mars.

It is a research and evidence-exploration platform, not a certified spacecraft fire-safety model, an operational firefighting system, or a source of operational safety instructions.
